clue.text: Grow into suit

definitions.meaning: to grow into something is to turn into it over time, as a boy turns into a man
to suit someone is to look good on them, as a hat flatters its wearer

explanation.surface: A child will grow into a suit bought a size too big.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one verb: to turn into, and to flatter or look right on someone.

clue.text: Call independent Northern Ireland painter

parts.note: to bell is an old word for to call or cry out, and a bell is also a call to church

explanation.surface: An independent painter from Northern Ireland is being summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian Renaissance painter, teacher of Titian.

clue.text: 20's resonance a feature of Celtic languages

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The ringing tone of a great bell is said to be characteristic of Celtic tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 's resonance' cut off the cross-reference: the definition is the whole phrase 20's resonance, the sound of BIG BEN (20 down).
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic sound is the noise a great clock bell makes when it strikes.

clue.text: PM's performance tense in headquarters

indicators.note: in puts the tense letter inside the other piece

parts.note: split as head, MAIN (as in main road, the chief one), plus quarters, EE, two east compass points
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister puts on a tense show at headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, afternoon. Read headquarters as head (MAIN) plus quarters (E and E, compass points); T goes inside after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is a theatre show given in the afternoon, the hours marked p.m.

clue.text: See 11
Light opera with no plot twists, causing exodus

indicators.note: twists says the remaining letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the pool
these letters are taken away from the pool before the rearranging

explanation.surface: A comic operetta with no turns in the story leads to an audience walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: With no takes P, L, O and T out of LIGHT OPERA, leaving IGHERA, which twists rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hegira is Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina in 622, a migration or departure.

clue.text: 15 aren't engaged in gossip

indicators.note: engaged, as cogs mesh together, says the letters are worked into one another

parts.note: 15 across is a little clang, the answer to that clue
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Bells that aren't ringing are busy chattering instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly, so continuous nattering is gossip.

clue.text: Row in golf club curtailed match celebration

indicators.note: in puts the noise inside the shortened club
curtailed means the last letter is cut off the club

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club
a din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: A quarrel at the golf club cut short the celebration of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests a sporting fixture at the golf club; here it is a marriage. Curtailed removes the club's last letter before the noise goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding celebrates a match in the sense of a marriage.

clue.text: Steptoe's cry topped first of Lord's seasonal line?

indicators.note: topped means the head letter is cut off the call

parts.note: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about rag-and-bone men, whose call to householders is a plea to bring out old junk

explanation.surface: A junk dealer's call is capped by the opening of a cricket ground's seasonal song.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's looks like the cricket ground; it is Lord Tennyson, whose New Year poem Ring Out, Wild Bells has this phrase as the first part of a line. Topped removes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The words open Tennyson's line about New Year bells sending off the year that is ending.

clue.text: Stoker's back from Spanish resort, leaving girl

indicators.note: from says that run is taken away from the resort

parts.note: Marbella is a resort on the Costa del Sol

indicators.note: back says the first name is turned round

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula

explanation.surface: A ship's stoker returns from a Spanish holiday town after leaving his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Back turns BRAM into MARB, the first four letters of MARBELLA; removing them leaves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's name, as in Ella Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Training nights also covering day's agenda

indicators.note: training, as a vine is trained into shape, says the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: covering says the second word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: too means also
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Evening training sessions also take in a day's list of tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: Day's gives D, the standard abbreviation; the apostrophe s is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items that need attention, the jobs still waiting.

clue.text: Winning three set out, appearing after 8

indicators.note: set out says the letters are laid out afresh in another order

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A winning trio is arranged, following the eighth.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is RING OUT THE OLD; Tennyson's line continues with this phrase, so it comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's New Year line pairs sending off the old year with welcoming the next, so this phrase follows the 8 down phrase.

clue.text: Bush in suitable place, one assumed originally

parts.note: a garden is a fitting place for a shrub to grow
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A shrub is in the right spot, one would have assumed at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Bird in illuminated tableau left by a British king

parts.note: lit means illuminated

indicators.note: left by says that pair departs from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are removed
A as written plus B, the abbreviation for British
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A bird appears in a lit-up stage scene, abandoned by a British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Left by takes A and B out of TABLEAU, leaving TLEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: The little auk is a small black and white Arctic seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: As conductor may comment on note: "I mean it!"

definitions.text: As conductor may comment on note
definitions.meaning: an orchestra conductor might remark that a note was sung or played too low
an emphatic declaration that a statement is final and not open to debate

explanation.surface: A conductor's remark on a note doubles as a firm insistence.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means both below pitch and absolute or downright, as in a flat refusal.

clue.text: Can good come of a little 2?

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Could something good come from a small amount of noise?
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is CLANG, so a little 2 is a small ringing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A ting is a light high ringing sound, a small version of a loud metallic ring.

clue.text: Basis of economy in China more sound than 15

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the friend

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means pal

indicators.note: basis of means the starting point, the first letter, of the next word

explanation.surface: The foundation of China's economy is stronger than a tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound here is a noun, not healthy; 15 is TING, and a full ring of bells makes more noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a loud ringing of a set of bells, much fuller than a small ting.

clue.text: Yank hosts exceptionally rich English barman

indicators.note: hosts says the first piece holds the others inside

parts.note: to yank is to pull

indicators.note: read as with exceptions, every other letter of the word is skipped

explanation.surface: An American welcomes a very wealthy English bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: Barman is the composer Henry Purcell, a writer of bars of music, with a hint that barmen pull pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was an English Baroque composer, a man whose music is written in bars.

clue.text: Scottish team faces local team as outsiders

indicators.note: faces are the fronts, so take the leading letter of each word

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, the home side for a Scottish reader

explanation.surface: A Scottish football side takes on the neighbourhood club in a match against visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangers are people from elsewhere, not belonging to the group.

clue.text: Great Lake too reduced in extent

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside

parts.note: area is extent

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: A large lake has shrunk too much in size.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true as well: the Aral Sea has shrunk badly since its feeder rivers were diverted for irrigation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, was once among the largest lakes on earth.

clue.text: Red plum duff not ordered

indicators.note: duff is slang for useless or broken, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A red plum that has gone bad is simply out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpled means crumpled and untidy, so in disarray.

clue.text: Striker's being replaced after bad start

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow that opening letter
start means take the opening letter of the word
replaced says the letters are put back in a different place

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer is being substituted after making a poor start to the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Striker suggests a footballer; it is the great bell that strikes the hours at Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Ben is the great bell in the Palace of Westminster clock tower that strikes the hours.

clue.text: Stir nuts into evergreen mint

indicators.note: into puts the jumbled letters inside the tree

parts.note: a pine is an evergreen tree

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to mix nuts into an evergreen herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Mint looks like the herb; it means unused, as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: In mint condition means as new and unspoilt, which is pristine.

clue.text: In the style of eg Titanic wake-up calls?

parts.note: a la is French for in the manner of
RMS stands for Royal Mail Ship, the prefix of the Titanic

explanation.surface: A doom-laden ship's style of rousing its passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarms are bells or signals that rouse sleepers, as an alarm clock does.

clue.text: One of The Three Bells in W3

definitions.meaning: ... Bell was the pen name of Anne Bronte, alongside her sisters Currer and Ellis Bell
W3 is the postcode of a district of west London

explanation.surface: One of three bells is found in a London postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: The district in west London covered by the W3 postcode, and the Bronte pseudonym.

clue.text: They go 15 etc for you but not for me, dammit!

definitions.text: They go 15 etc for you but not for me
definitions.meaning: a First World War song says the bells of hell go ting-a-ling-a-ling for you but not for me

explanation.surface: Soldiers sing of bells that ring for others but not for them, with a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild British oath of exasperation and also the bells in the old soldiers' song.

clue.text: Tax loss

definitions.meaning: a charge paid to use a road or bridge
the cost in lives or damage, as in death count

explanation.surface: A levy amounts to a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a fee for passage, and also the damage or casualties an event causes.

clue.text: Ship's bell's old first note falls within range

indicators.note: falls within puts the note inside

parts.note: a line is a range, as of goods
ut was the old name for the first note of the scale, now do

explanation.surface: A ship's bell's first note used to fall within a certain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The bell of HMS Lutine hangs at Lloyd's of London, rung for news of lost ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lutine Bell, salvaged from the frigate Lutine, hangs in the Lloyd's insurance building.

clue.text: Wizard of Oz Dorothy initially cautioned

parts.note: Shane Warne was the Australian spin-bowling wizard of cricket, Oz being slang for Australia

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Dorothy was first cautioned by the Wizard of Oz.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wizard of Oz is not the film's magician but the Australian cricketer Shane Warne.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warned is to be cautioned about a danger.
